criteria.text: list --priority shows the most urgent task first
criteria.quote: `add TEXT --priority N` stores the task with priority N, where N is 1, 2 or 3 (1 is the most urgent).

criteria.text: a task added without --priority gets priority 2
criteria.quote: A task added without `--priority` gets priority 2.
criteria.then: it prints `3 [ ] high`, `2 [ ] plain`, `1 [ ] low` in that order

criteria.text: tasks with the same priority keep id order
criteria.quote: tasks with the same priority stay in id order
criteria.then: it prints `2 [ ] y`, `1 [ ] x`, `3 [ ] z` in that order

criteria.text: done marks a task done and confirms
criteria.quote: `done ID` marks the task as done in the file and prints `done ID`
criteria.then: it prints `done 1` and task 1 is stored with done true

criteria.text: remove deletes a task and confirms
criteria.quote: `remove ID` deletes the task from the file and prints `removed ID`
criteria.then: it prints `removed 1` and only task 2 is left in the file

criteria.quote: For an unknown ID, `done` and `remove` print `error: no task ID` to standard error and exit with code 1
criteria.then: it prints `error: no task 99` to standard error and exits with code 2

criteria.text: add stores an open task and prints its id
criteria.quote: `add TEXT` stores a new open task and prints `added ID`
criteria.then: it prints `added 1` and exits with code 0

criteria.text: list prints one line per task in id order with its done mark
criteria.quote: `list` prints one line per task in id order: `ID [ ] TEXT` for an open task and `ID [x] TEXT` for a done task.
criteria.given: a file with open task 1 `a` and done task 2 `b`

criteria.text: list on an empty file prints nothing
criteria.quote: `list` on an empty file prints nothing and exits with code 0
criteria.then: it prints nothing and exits with code 0

rules.quote: Ids start at 1 and are never reused

rules.text: Error messages go to standard error, normal output to standard output
rules.quote: Normal output goes to standard output; error messages go to standard error.
